## 5573cf8e2aa4

**A5573-1 — Reproduced teaching shortcut / documented geometry limitation.**
The wrong rule “for each output column, paint cyan from the first occupied panel
row through the last” fits every usable canonical pair and every generated draw
in this focused probe. The current construction cannot teach against this rival:
`_assemble` occupies one uninterrupted interval of `_snake_cells`, which traverses
whole rows or whole columns and may reverse direction. Every such interval has
contiguous occupied rows within each column. This construction argument applies
to its valid overrides as well as default draws; the finite measurements below
are separately reported.

The retained hand-constructed witness has an eight-cell ring as the union of two
overlapping, individually monochrome, connected panel paths. Input: **5 rows × 11
columns.** Output: **5 rows × 5 columns.** Racket leaves the center `(2, 2)` blank;
the column-span rival paints it cyan, producing exactly one wrong cell. The input
passes `self_check`, including exact metadata `{grid_h: 5, half_w: 5,
palette_size: 1, relation_profile: "sparse"}`. Relation counts are 17 both-blank,
3 left-only, 3 right-only, and 2 same-color overlaps. It satisfies the declared
axes and invariants, but is **outside the actual row/column-snake construction's
reachable support**. The notes already acknowledge restricted geometry. This is
a concrete teaching consequence of that limitation, not a generated-label
failure or an ambiguous answer to one of the tested generated queries.

### Measured evidence

All counts below use the unchanged generator SHA shown below and Racket labels
from the supported public `apply` command.

| Probe | Result / denominator |
|---|---|
| Canonical fit of the column-span rival | 3/3 usable pairs: variant 0, train 0 and 1, test 0 |
| Default generated fit | 36/36 draws: seeds `0, 1, 23`, each difficulty `easy, medium, hard`, sample indices `0..3`, no overrides |
| Override generated fit | 6/6 draws: seed `23`, sample `5`, difficulty `medium`, `grid_h=5`, `half_w=5`, both palette sizes crossed with all three actual `RELATION_PROFILES` |
| Unique generated inputs | 30 unique inputs among the 42 generated draws; repeated grids are retained and not counted as unique |
| Racket execution and Python-mirror parity | 46/46 valid outputs and agreements: 3 canonical + 42 generated + 1 ring |
| Validator acceptance | 46/46 inputs accepted |
| Ordered lessons | Column-span rival survives all 9/9 windows with demonstrations `0,1,2` and query `3` |
| Query rotations | Survives 36/36 placements: each of the four positions as query in each window; remaining demonstrations stay in sample order |
| Existing named-rival hook | Reports no reasons for 36/36 placements; the new column-span rival is undeclared |
| Focused existing task suite | 12 tests passed, exit 0 |

The lesson counts use the nine seed/difficulty combinations above and three
demonstrations per window. They are overlapping reuse of the same grids, not an
additional sample census. No arbitrary-start lesson census is claimed. The rival
agrees with every tested generated query (`survived_all`); its wrong answer is
demonstrated by the separate, validator-accepted ring.

The probe iterates the source's actual `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and
`LESSON_COMPETITORS` declarations. Only `raw_cell_inequality` fits all 3/3
canonical pairs; occupancy XOR fits 1/3, intersection and each copy-side rival
fit 0/3. These are recorded as candidate-fit results, not as a separate defect.

**Suggested follow-up:** introduce a vertical-gap witness such as the ring while
preserving the desired connected-object scale, and declare the column-span
rival. Keeping the present construction should carry the explicit limitation
that lessons do not distinguish exact occupancy from vertical span filling.
No source or authority was changed during this findings-only audit.

### Source identity and reproduction

- Generator SHA-256: `741c159b6ea59db191c59de14107e63bb8eef78c994996e9318d463f8c2746a9`.
- Canonical program UTF-8 SHA-256: `59a18f0cd9d4ef4c9dfce130b45f162be0d75123f1c20202f316a9d8d644d81f`; selected rule hash `59a18f0cd9d4`.
- Executed rule-text SHA-256 recorded by public `apply`: `38787efbd62bf4a3c38d9bfae25bd9736ffd1f256ff714308ce37bfdf8984084`.
- Evidence: `checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/counterexample.json` contains the input,
  actual Racket output, rival output, one-cell disagreement, validation result,
  domain caveat, hashes, and exact command. `racket.json` contains all 46 executed
  results; the ring is input index 45. `prepared.json` records every seed/index/
  override; `report.json` records comparisons, canonical fit, and lessons.
- Reproducer: `checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/probe.py`. `commands.json` records all
  four substantive commands with working directories, exit codes and evidence.

From `packet_root` (the extracted `WORK` directory), all three commands exited 0:

```bash
python3 checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/probe.py prepare --repo repo
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 5573cf8e2aa4 --input ../checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/input.json --out ../checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/racket.json
python3 checks/audit/5573cf8e2aa4/probe.py verify --repo repo
```

The Racket wrapper's effective working directory was
`/workspace/scratch/68d64d7e9f75/packet/WORK/repo`. The focused test command was
`python3 generators/5573cf8e2aa4/tests/test_generator_5573cf8e2aa4.py`, run from
`repo`, exit 0. No broad battery or private solve artifacts were inspected.
